title: ENARA Experiment 5c - pre-registration (does the plan/engine arbitration add anything? one third of the Experiment 5b size)
note: AI-simulated students only; not evidence about real learners. Locked before any run. This experiment tests the owner's ship bar: ENARA must clearly beat the plain AI tutor.
design: Matched triplets as in Experiments 4-5b; evidence-seeded learners (as in 5b); 17 NEW students (new seed) x 6 areas x 1 replication = 102 triplets (one third of 5b's 300) on the 16 hold-out outcomes; 4 items per stage; 3 answer samples per item; deterministic scoring; blind judge sample.

conditions.A: ENARA with ENARA_ENGINE_V2=all (wrongAnswer, belief, memory, cache), arbitration OFF - the Experiment 5b ENARA arm
conditions.B: ENARA with ENARA_ENGINE_V2=all,arbitration - differs from A in exactly one switch
conditions.C: plain AI tutor with the same school record as text (as in 5b)

holdout.disclosure: The 16 hold-out outcomes were already scored under A, B (research flag) and C in Experiment 4, so aggregate results on them were seen; their transcripts were not read. The v2 changes were designed from code review plus Experiment 2-4 aggregate and transcript evidence on development outcomes. New students and a new seed are used, so no Experiment 4 block is reused.

primaryOutcome: Learning gain (post minus pre proportion correct on independent deterministic assessments).
secondaryOutcomes: input tokens and cache-read tokens per tutor call
sampleSize: 102 triplets by owner request (one third of 300). Power: with a per-triplet gain-difference variance of about 0.15 (Experiments 4-5b), 80% power at alpha 0.025 needs a true effect of about 0.12 (12 points) or more (n = 9.505 * sigma2 / delta^2 -> delta = sqrt(9.505*0.15/102) = 0.118). A null result therefore says nothing about effects smaller than about 12 points; the study is a screening test, not a decisive one.
inference: Two-way (student x outcome) cluster bootstrap 95% CI; sign-flip permutation test on per-student mean differences; Holm-Bonferroni over the two confirmatory contrasts; Benjamini-Hochberg for exploratory contrasts; paired d_z with Hedges correction.
shipBar: Not a ship decision. B is worth carrying into a full-size confirmatory run only if B-A is positive with a 95% CI excluding 0, or the point estimate is at least +0.08 with Holm-adjusted p < 0.2 (screening threshold, declared in advance). The owner's bar for shipping (ENARA clearly beats the plain tutor, Holm p < 0.05, CI excludes 0) is unchanged and applies to the full-size run.
decisionRules: B better than A (or C) only if Holm-adjusted p < 0.05 and the CI excludes 0; the screening rule above decides only whether a full-size run is justified. Failed or incomplete blocks stay in the data.
knownLimits: Screening size (about 12-point minimum detectable effect). Single-session simulation; memory cannot act. Hold-out outcomes were already scored in Experiments 4 and 5b (aggregates seen); this run uses new students and seed, and the same 16 outcomes.

evidenceSeeding.rule: From the hidden learner state (identical for A, B and C): knowsAlready -> mastery status proficient (estimate 0.8, 4 evidence items, 3 independent); otherwise -> status emerging (0.3) plus, when the learner holds a misconception, a confirmed mistaken-idea record whose text is the benchmark misconception description (never an assessment item).
evidenceSeeding.A_B: seeded into the throwaway database as StudentObjectiveMastery and StudentMisconception records, as the school's system would hold them (the same mapping the fixture harness uses)
evidenceSeeding.C: the plain tutor receives the same record as one sentence of text in its prompt (a deliberately generous baseline: the plain tutor is given the information, so ENARA wins only through what it does with it)
evidenceSeeding.probe: With seeding, the plan changes: emerging + misconception -> direct_instruction + worked_example; proficient -> mastery_learning + elaborative_interrogation; without seeding -> formative_feedback + retrieval_practice (NO_EVIDENCE).
